reason: (1) The append-only refusal is trigger a00_phase_c_refund_decision_immutable on public.phase_c_refund_decision (BEFORE DELETE OR UPDATE FOR EACH ROW, function fn_phase_c_refund_decision_immutable); the table holds 0 rows, so there is nothing to rewrite. (2) A real founder session CAN be driven from this repository without the founder acting: measured 24 Aug 2026 in an aborted transaction, fn_phase_c_founder_subject_bind(<auth_user_id of management@quotesdone.com>) returned ok=true as current_user postgres (it refuses only anon and authenticated), and fn_phase_c_require_founder(null) then returned 'management@quotesdone.com'. The blocker is therefore not reachability — it is his standing rule that a fixture may never forge a founder decision, plus kernel_write_authority holding 0 rows for phase_c_refund_decision, so a00_kernel_write_guard refuses every write to it.
what_would_make_it_executable: A committed founder decision the founder himself made, and a route registered in public.kernel_write_authority for phase_c_refund_decision so a decision row can exist at all. Then the injection is an UPDATE or DELETE of that row and a00_phase_c_refund_decision_immutable answers. Nothing in this harness may create the subject.

reason: Measured over pg_proc in public: five routines take a claim. fn_phase_c_outbox_claim claims public.phase_c_event_outbox rows (pending/retry_wait, next_attempt_at <= now) FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; fn_kernel_outbox_deliver claims the same relation plus rows stuck 'claimed' over 15 minutes, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, then DELIVERS externally; fn_workflow_step_claim claims workflow step-run rows FOR UPDATE OF sr SKIP LOCKED; fn_assign_founding_rank takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('qd_founding_rank')) over the founding-rank counter; fn_phase_c_event_binding_status only NAMES 'FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED' in a documentation string and claims nothing. All unusable here: SKIP LOCKED shows only when a second session locks a COMMITTED row, every probe is one aborted transaction, and the outbox is served by live cron phase_c_outbox_deliver_1min, so a committed row sends for real within 60s.
what_would_make_it_executable: Two committed connections against a committed subject, under a provider mode that cannot send. Concretely: a claimable relation whose consumer is fixture-only, plus a harness opening two sessions so one holds the row lock while the other calls the claimer, and an assertion that the second session claims 0 rows. Under the zero-effect hold the outbox cannot be that relation.

reason: public.inquiries holds 0 rows; creating one fires trg_inquiry_received_a (function trg_inquiry_received, verified present) which starts a real W05 run whose trace rows cannot then be removed. Proved by execution 24 Aug 2026 in an aborted transaction: DELETE FROM public.phase_c_system_execution WHERE trace_id = 2757 raised 'phase_c_system_execution is append-only: DELETE on trace 2757 refused. An execution record that can be edited after the fact records the editor, not the execution.' (trigger z10_phase_c_system_execution_append_only, BEFORE DELETE OR UPDATE FOR EACH ROW). Setting kernel.maintenance_reason gave the identical refusal — no maintenance door. DELETE on public.phase_c_trace was refused earlier still by FK phase_c_trace_parent_trace_id_fkey. Both are the frozen Phase C subject 'trace_ledger'; 5166 and 5403 rows.
what_would_make_it_executable: A tear-down path for a fixture inquiry that the trace ledger accepts — either a fixture-scoped trace partition the append-only trigger exempts by construction, or a section-8 probe using an inquiry the business genuinely owns and never deleting it. Today deleting the residue is impossible, so the inquiry must never be committed.

reason: No Phase D path renders a supplier-facing message body: of the fn_phase_d_* routines, none produces a rendered document, and public.phase_d_acceptance_document is a four-column registry (object_id, document_slug, why, registered_at), not a rendering. Worse, and measured 24 Aug 2026 by execution: fn_phase_d_external_deliver('W13-S02', approved_payload with body 'Dear supplier, contact Ahmad at zz.cust@example.invalid / 0501234567') returned ok=true, delivered=true and recorded attempt 25981 — the delivery door does not screen the body it is handed, and its source contains no match for br-011, PII or 'customer identity'. BR-011 IS enforced and does refuse exactly that string (see PD-PRIV-001), but only where a caller hands the payload to fn_phase_d_rule_check, and the send path does not.
what_would_make_it_executable: fn_phase_d_external_deliver calling fn_phase_d_rule_check('BR-011', jsonb_build_object('supplier_payload', <the rendered body>)) before it records an attempt, and refusing on ENFORCED_FAIL. That single call turns this into an injection with a control: the same delivery with the identity removed must still deliver. Flagged as an open hole, not merely an untestable case.

reason: A re-emission needs a consumer that both consumes and emits, observed twice on one event. Measured: public.phase_b_event holds 347 events of which 54 have emitted_by = primary_consumer_role_id (the recorded self-loops), but that is a static registry property, not a runtime consumption. The only live consumer of public.phase_c_event_outbox (33 rows) is cron job phase_c_outbox_deliver_1min — active, schedule '* * * * *', command 'select public.fn_kernel_outbox_deliver(25, ''cron:phase_c_outbox_deliver_1min'')' — which runs in its own transaction outside this one and delivers externally. So committing an outbox row to watch it be consumed would send a real external effect within 60 seconds, and inside an aborted transaction the cron never sees the row, so no consumption and no re-emission can occur.
what_would_make_it_executable: A consumer callable in-transaction under provider_mode 'mock' that re-emits, plus an emission ledger keyed on (event, source attempt) so a second emission is countable rather than inferred. With those, the injection is one call and the control is the same call on an event whose consumer does not emit.

reason: The subject does not exist in this estate. Measured: public.phase_d_object_state_contract holds 0 object_ids matching draw|redact|metadata, and public.phase_d_object_write_map (22 rows) binds no drawing revision or redaction-approval relation. The nearest live rule is BR-035 (br035_unapproved_revision_published), whose predicate compares approved_revision_ref with publishing_revision_ref and resolves the ref against IMMUTABLE_REVISION records in public.phase_d_object_record; it reads no redaction state at all, so scoring this defect on BR-035 would be a refusal about a different fact. File revision state and redaction approval are storage plus document-pipeline facts and neither is represented in the database.
what_would_make_it_executable: A registered business object for a drawing revision carrying its redaction-approval state, and a predicate that reads it. Then the injection is publishing a revision whose redaction is unapproved, and the control is the same revision with the redaction approved by an independent reviewer.

reason: Hidden metadata is a property of a rendered file, and no Phase D routine renders one: of the fn_phase_d_* routines in public, none produces a PDF, DOCX or image, and public.phase_d_acceptance_document is a registry of slugs (object_id, document_slug, why, registered_at) rather than an artefact store. The section 8 HTTP harness that could have carried this ran 23 probes on 2026-08-23 (public.phase_d_section8_probe_result) and none of them scans an artefact's embedded metadata; public.phase_d_section8_defect_map maps 11 defects and PD-PRIV-005 is not one of them. There is therefore no object to strip and no scanner to refuse it.
what_would_make_it_executable: A rendering path that produces a supplier-facing file plus a metadata scanner over the produced bytes (EXIF/XMP/document properties) invoked before the file is exposed. The injection is a file whose author or comment fields carry the customer identity; the control is the same render with the fields cleared.

reason: The distinction the defect asks for is not representable. Measured on the live body of public.fn_phase_d_gate_evaluate: it contains ZERO 'exception when' handlers, so a read error inside it (permission denied, relation missing) is not converted into a verdict — it propagates and aborts the caller's transaction. There is no state, refusal_code or evidence_absent value that says 'the gate could not read', as distinct from the BLOCKED/false it returns when it read and judged. Provoking the read error itself would also need a grant revoked or a relation renamed on production; the function is STABLE with SET search_path TO public, pg_temp and runs as the owner of every relation it reads, so nothing a caller can set inside an aborted transaction reaches it.
what_would_make_it_executable: An exception handler in fn_phase_d_gate_evaluate returning state 'BLOCKED' with a distinct refusal code such as gate_read_failed, plus one relation the gate reads that a test context can make unreadable in-transaction. Then the injection is that relation being unreadable and the control is the identical call with it readable.

reason: The refusal does not exist and the subject is outside the database. Measured 24 Aug 2026: no file in scripts/checks/ and no job in .github/workflows/ (checks.yml, deploy-functions.yml, project-parity.yml, resilience-ping.yml) scans supabase/functions for a direct provider client; the nearest check, scripts/checks/llm_gateway_credential.test.mjs, asserts about supabase/functions/_shared/llm.ts and its importers, which is the gateway module, not a bypass of it. A plain grep for openrouter.ai|api.openai.com|api.anthropic.com over supabase/functions today matches 5 files (ai_gateway, ai_health, cost_snapshot, designer, resend_inbound) and nothing in CI refuses any of them. A SQL function cannot read the repository, so fn_phase_d_run_injected_defects can never execute this case; PD-PROV-001 covers the database half by scanning pg_proc.
what_would_make_it_executable: A CI test that fails when a file under supabase/functions other than ai_gateway calls a provider host directly, and a recorded result table the SQL runner can read — the same shape as public.phase_d_section8_probe_result. The injection is a deliberate bypass added on a branch; the control is the same function routed through _shared/llm.ts.

reason: NOT DISCRIMINATED at the layer this harness can reach. Measured: public.quotes has row security enabled (relrowsecurity = true) and ZERO policies (pg_policy over 'public.quotes'::regclass returns 0 rows), so every non-bypassing role — supplier A and supplier B alike — sees and updates nothing. A control that differs in exactly one respect therefore behaves identically, which answers nothing about the defect. There is also no SQL entry point to test instead: no routine in public whose source touches public.quotes resolves a supplier from auth.uid() (measured: 0). The decision lives in an edge function. The section 8 harness that ran 23 probes on 2026-08-23 covered the analogous supplier settings write (probe P2-cross-write: A named B's id, the write landed on A's own row and B was unchanged) but nothing about quotes, and there are 0 quotes on the estate.
what_would_make_it_executable: A section 8 probe with two real supplier bearers and two committed quotes, one per supplier, asserting that A's edit of B's quote changes no row of B's and that A's edit of A's own quote does. Under the hold that needs committed quotes, which the marketplace does not currently have.

reason: The instrument measures a different subject and the fact is not stored. Measured on the live bodies: BR-019 ('Published quote visibility only') and GATE-018 both evaluate exactly count(*) from public.quote_comparisons where id = comparison_id AND customer_id = caller_customer_id — ownership, never publication. And there is no publication state to read: 0 columns matching publish|visib exist on public.quote_comparisons (id, inquiry_id, customer_id, lang, quote_count, signature, analysis, created_at) or on public.quotes. So an unpublished comparison belonging to the caller passes both, and injecting 'unpublished' changes nothing a control could distinguish. public.quotes additionally has RLS on with 0 policies, so the portal read cannot be reproduced in SQL.
what_would_make_it_executable: A published/visible state on the comparison a customer reads, and a BR-019 predicate that reads it as well as ownership. Then the injection is a customer reading their own unpublished comparison and the control is the same customer reading the published one.

reason: The rule that names this defect tests a self-declaration, not the overwrite. Measured on the live body of fn_phase_d_rule_check: BR-018 is v_ok := coalesce(btrim(p_context->>'quote_revision_ref'),'') <> '' AND coalesce(p_context->>'platform_edited','true') = 'false'. It never compares a stored original with a normalised value, so a normalisation that actually overwrote the supplier's figure and reported platform_edited='false' passes, and the only thing an injection can flip is the caller's own claim about itself. There is also nothing to overwrite: the normalisation path is not built, and public.phase_d_object_write_map binds quotation to public.quotes with no separate normalised projection.
what_would_make_it_executable: A normalisation path that writes a normalised projection alongside the supplier's immutable quotation_revision, and a BR-018 predicate comparing the two records rather than reading a flag. Then the injection is a normalisation that changes the original and the control is one that changes only the projection.

reason: Injecting a missing successor owner means editing public.phase_b_workflow_step, which carries trigger z90_phase_b_freeze (function fn_phase_b_freeze_guard) alongside a10_phase_b_owner_guard. The step registry is founder-approved and frozen (tag phase-b-founder-approved-2026-08-15); z90 compares a digest, not a count, so blanking one accountable_role_id is refused even though no row count moves, and getting past it requires a formal Phase B change request with app.phase_b_change_reason set in the same transaction. A change request raised only to make a defect harness go green would be the fabrication the founder's rules forbid.
what_would_make_it_executable: A fixture-scoped copy of the step registry that the kernel's successor resolution reads in a test context, so a successor with no owner can exist without touching the frozen table. Alternatively a founder-approved PBCR that deliberately adds one unowned successor as a permanent negative control.

reason: The subject is a kernel-owned table and Phase D has no door to it. Measured: fn_phase_d_object_write refuses by name — 'is written by the frozen kernel (%). A Phase D handler that wrote it would be a second creator for one object. Use fn_kernel_step_complete. (pd_object_kernel_owned)' — and public.kernel_write_authority names only fn_kernel_cancel, fn_kernel_open_step, fn_kernel_step_complete, fn_kernel_workflow_start and fn_phase_c_step_run_trace_subject as writers of public.phase_c_workflow_step_run, so a00_kernel_write_guard refuses a raw INSERT. Every one of those kernel routines writes the trace as part of the same call, so an active step run without a trace cannot be produced through any door, and doing it raw would be a test of the kernel rather than of Phase D.
what_would_make_it_executable: A kernel test hook that opens a step run with tracing suppressed, so the trace-required guard has something to refuse. Absent that, this is a kernel invariant proved by construction rather than an injectable Phase D defect.

reason: As PD-TRACE-001, and with the closing half additionally unreachable. Reaching a terminal object with an open trace means writing public.phase_c_workflow_step_run, which fn_phase_d_object_write refuses as kernel-owned (pd_object_kernel_owned) and for which public.kernel_write_authority names only the five kernel routines, so a00_kernel_write_guard refuses a raw write. Closing the trace is also an append-only operation: proved by execution 24 Aug 2026, DELETE on public.phase_c_system_execution is refused unconditionally by z10_phase_c_system_execution_append_only even with kernel.maintenance_reason set, and DELETE on public.phase_c_trace is refused by FK phase_c_trace_parent_trace_id_fkey. Both are the frozen Phase C subject 'trace_ledger'.
what_would_make_it_executable: A kernel test hook that terminates an object while deliberately leaving its trace open, in a transaction the harness can abort. Only the kernel can create that state, so only the kernel can offer the hook.

reason: The read-only trace exemption is a kernel registry fact scored by a board, not a write-time refusal an injection can provoke. Measured 24 Aug 2026: public.fn_kernel_system_trace_state() reports 'state_changing_components_on_a_read_only_policy' as '0 of 23' (ok) and 'read_only_components_without_a_recorded_exemption' as '0 of 23'; the policy itself is TRACE-MONITORING in public.phase_c_trace_policy, scoped to read-only health probes. Moving a state-changing component onto that policy is an edit of the kernel's component registry — no Phase D routine writes it, and fn_phase_d_object_write refuses kernel-owned relations (pd_object_kernel_owned) — so Phase D has no path that even requests the exemption.
what_would_make_it_executable: A Phase D-callable request for a trace exemption on a named component, so the kernel can refuse it in the same transaction and a control (a genuinely read-only component) can be granted one. Today the only instrument is an after-the-fact board over committed components.

reason: There is no stale source to assert from and no freshness check to refuse it. Measured 24 Aug 2026: public.legal_documents holds 12 rows (complaints-policy, disclaimer, information-security-policy, kyc-policy, anti-bribery-policy, cookie-policy, acceptable-use, data-retention-policy, privacy, supplier-agreement, customer-terms, refund-policy) and none of them is a tax or legal-interpretation source; a repository grep for 'corporate tax' across .md and .ts files returns 0 files. The table carries effective_date and updated_at but no routine compares either against now(), so nothing in the estate can judge a legal artefact stale. BR-025 reads legal_documents for version and hash equality only.
what_would_make_it_executable: A registered tax/legal interpretation artefact carrying a review-by date, and a predicate that refuses an assertion resting on one past that date. Then the injection is a claim citing the expired artefact and the control is the identical claim citing the current one.
